findings.reason: as written the repair cannot clear the case its own bullet 1 quotes, so the plan must record the host per attempt (or sweep every host's copy once the run is terminal) or it ships a fix whose own evidence still leaks.
findings.text: the change records one host per run, but a run gets a scratch directory named for its run id on every host an attempt ran on, so the recorded host's removal leaves every other attempt's copy; this is exactly the cited evidence, where 5,014 bytes were removed on one host while 172 KB from later attempts survives on another

findings.reason: with no named production caller the debt is recorded and never settled, so the node would have to modify a landed section's pass without the plan saying so, and the existing reaper must be extended or the claim dropped.
findings.text: "The §7 sweep, run on that host, settles the debt" names a caller that does not do this: `retention_sweep` in reckon/crew/gc.py:1329 runs run-directory retention and, per §7, "runs the run-directory retention alone, not the rest of gc", while the only scratch reaper, `garbage_collect_orphan_scratch` (gc.py:1030), is reached from `garbage_collect` and deliberately withholds a resumable run's scratch

findings.reason: a control that cannot fail is the thing the rubric exists to catch, and the fixture needs a same-named scratch on the release host (which is also the real shape) to redden it.
findings.text: the negative control is inert as specified: with the release host holding no directory of the run's name, the mutated release (removing on its own host whichever host made the scratch) removes nothing and still reports not-removed, so the second case passes unchanged

findings.reason: the plan already sends the node to find the route that skipped the release, so the sentence is a loose claim about code the node inspects rather than an instruction it would follow wrongly.
findings.text: "Every completion path already calls `_release_after_promotion`" is contradicted by the plan's own bullet 3, which reports 13 review and plan-review runs with no release block at all

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `remove_worker_scratch` resolves at reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:829, `_release_after_promotion` at reckon/crew/promotion.py:1125 and 1752, reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:188 and reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2590; the four hrefs resolve once `.html` is appended (monitor-storage-load-rca, history-persists-as-detail-washes-out, the-crew-home-has-a-bound, evidence/archive/crew-state-stays-bounded-landed all exist).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §8's declared negative control (plan.html:170) cannot redden the case it is attached to, because the second case's release host is given no same-named scratch to remove.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §8 puts gate logs under the run directory and names the committed evidence fragment as the durable record, the same disposition already given to §6: the fragment is committed and must quote each gate's command and summary line.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §8 introduces no symbol, filename or comment carrying a plan label, stage name or ticket number; "§7 sweep" is a reference between plan sections, not a name entering code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8 keys the host to the run while the failure the plan cites is per attempt across hosts, and it names the §7 sweep as the caller that settles a cross-host debt when §7 as landed runs the run-directory retention alone and touches no scratch.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 has one goal (a run's scratch leaves with the run, on the host that made it); the review-promotion clause is one of the routes to that same goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` records `s8:["crew-state-stays-bounded#s7"]` and s7 exists and is declared done, which is the ordering §8 needs; no relationship points at a wrong node.
